Sample Name: General Medicine Followup - Chronic Pain and Substance Use
Description: Chronic back and extremity pain, recurrent pediculosis, and active substance use.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: The patient reports persistent low back pain, occasionally extending toward the neck, along with intermittent left arm and leg pain. He continues using heroin and has not yet enrolled in substance use treatment. The possibility of beginning an outpatient program before consideration of inpatient rehabilitation was discussed. He reports recurrent head lice after reuse of a shared comb. He has also had intermittent reflux symptoms, hard stools, and nocturia two to three times nightly. He has previously used ibuprofen 600 mg for pain. Cigarette smoking continues.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: Left arm pain could not be reproduced consistently by movement or palpation during examination. No definite acute injection-site infection was identified in the discussion.
LABORATORY DATA: Previously reported LDL cholesterol 111 and HDL 52.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
1. Heroin use: Counseled concerning treatment and referral to the outpatient substance use program, with possible subsequent inpatient treatment if appropriate. Advised urgent evaluation for any red, swollen, hot, or painful injection site.
2. Chronic back and extremity pain: Renew ibuprofen 600 mg as discussed; definitive interventions deferred pending substance use treatment and further evaluation.
3. Recurrent head lice: Prescribe NIX hair treatment and review avoidance of reinfestation.
4. Gastroesophageal reflux: Renew omeprazole.
5. Constipation: Encourage fluids and dietary fiber.
6. Nocturia and prostate concerns: Discussed screening risks and benefits. No prostate cancer screening was recommended at this encounter given the reported risk profile.
Follow up in six months or sooner as needed.
